correctness.rationale: The radical decomposes into length 1 (A+B+C), length 2 (A⊗B+B⊗C), and length 3 (A⊗B⊗C) path spaces. Vanishing of the commutator yields exactly two adjacent tensor equations and one length-three equation. For endpoint-pair ranks i,j, the last equation is a surjective map onto (<a,a_prime>⊗B⊗C)+(A⊗B⊗<c,c_prime>), of rank s(it+rj-ij), leaving q^(D-E) choices. Partitioning middle pair by ranks 0,1,2 gives precisely the three displayed terms and free longest-path factor q^(2rst). Independent direct small-case values are 1024,41553,30208,108544 for (q,r,s,t)=(2,1,1,1),(3,1,1,1),(2,2,1,1),(2,1,2,1), respectively; all match the formula. The proof covers all prime powers, not only tested prime fields.
residual_risks: Positive r,s,t and all-ones projectives only; no arbitrary quiver or radical polynomiality claim
